name: f1-weekly-longform
description: Weekly long-form F1 video — research-backed, story-driven, retention-optimized

context.problem: Long-form videos average 26 views with 8-9% retention. Viewers leave after ~2 min on 17-22 min videos. Scripts are too long, topics lack depth for their duration, and narratives don't create enough tension to keep viewers watching.
context.goal: Produce one high-quality long-form video per week that achieves >30% audience retention and >500 views within 7 days. Build the long-form audience alongside the working Shorts strategy.
constraints: Channel has 274 subs — can't assume loyal audience, must earn every minute of watch time
Shorts audience (57K views/month) is the funnel — long-form topics should appeal to that same audience
Production budget: Gemini TTS (free), yt-dlp footage, stock images. No paid actors or custom shoots.
Must be completable in one Claude session including all iterations

phases.name: Topic Selection & Validation
phases.description: Find a topic with genuine depth that the Shorts audience cares about
tasks: Analyze top-performing Shorts from the past 30 days to identify themes the audience engages with
Propose 3 topic options with: title, angle, why it has 4-6 minutes of genuine story (not padding)
For each topic: outline the narrative conflict, stakes, and resolution
Select the topic with the strongest 'why should I keep watching?' through-line
acceptance_criteria: Topic directly relates to themes proven by Shorts analytics (driver drama, untold stories, surprising facts)
Story has a clear protagonist, conflict, and resolution — not just an information dump
4-6 minute duration target is justified by actual content depth, not repetition
Title uses curiosity gap pattern (proven by Shorts: 'The Man With More F1 Races Than Any Driver' got 12K views)

phases.name: Script Writing with Self-Review Loop
phases.description: Write and iterate on the script until it meets quality bar. This is the most critical phase.
tasks: Research topic thoroughly: official sources, quotes, statistics, lesser-known details
Write script.json following the f1-scriptwriting skill guidelines
Self-review against ALL acceptance criteria below
Rewrite any section that fails criteria — iterate up to 3 times
Add references for every factual claim
Run fact checker: python3 src/fact_checker.py --project {name} --web-search
acceptance_criteria: HOOK TEST: First 15 seconds must work as a standalone Short — would it stop a scroll?
TENSION TEST: Every 60 seconds has a question, conflict, or revelation that makes the viewer need to know what's next
PADDING TEST: Read each segment and ask 'does this move the story forward?' — if no, cut it
DURATION TEST: Total script word count is 600-900 words (targeting 4-6 min at ~150 wpm narration pace)
SEGMENT LENGTH TEST: No segment exceeds 80 words / ~30 seconds — long segments kill retention
VARIETY TEST: Script uses at least 3 different section types (cold_open, rising_action, climax, etc.)
CTA TEST: Final segment includes subscribe/follow CTA
TAG TEST: script.json includes 'tags' array with driver names, team names, and topic keywords (15+ tags)
SELF-REVIEW: After writing, re-read the entire script aloud mentally and mark any moment where attention wanders — those sections must be rewritten or cut
REFERENCE TEST: Every factual claim has a source in the references array

phases.name: Audio, Footage & Assembly
phases.description: Produce the video with quality gates at each step
tasks: Generate audio: python3 src/audio_generator.py --project {name}
Download footage: python3 src/footage_downloader.py --project {name} --google-search --validate
Validate ALL footage with Gemini vision: python3 src/gemini_vision_validator.py --project {name}
Fix any footage mismatches before assembly
Assemble: python3 src/image_video_assembler.py --project {name} --resolution hd
Run post-assembly validation checks
acceptance_criteria: All footage passes Gemini vision validation
No segment has footage that doesn't match the narration topic
Video duration is within 10% of audio duration
First 15 seconds play correctly (hook is not cut off)
No freeze frames or black screens between segments
Each segment's video is at least 80% of its audio duration

phases.name: Final Quality Review
phases.description: Review the assembled video against the original quality bar before upload
tasks: Verify final duration is 4-6 minutes
Verify title uses curiosity gap pattern, not generic description
Verify tags array has 15+ relevant tags
Verify description includes story summary, references, and hashtags
Present to user for final approval
acceptance_criteria: Duration: 4-6 minutes (HARD LIMIT — reject if outside this range)
Title: Uses curiosity/intrigue pattern, under 60 characters
Tags: 15+ tags including specific driver/team names mentioned in script
Description: Includes summary, source references, and hashtags
Audio/video sync: No drift > 0.5 seconds at any point

anti_patterns: DO NOT pad a 3-minute story to 10 minutes — if the story is 5 minutes, make it 5 minutes
DO NOT use generic topic titles like 'F1 Testing Recap' — use curiosity gaps
DO NOT skip the self-review loop — the script is 90% of the video quality
DO NOT create videos longer than 6 minutes until the channel has >1000 subscribers
DO NOT reuse the same hook pattern for every video
DO NOT upload without tags — this killed discoverability on all previous long-form videos
DO NOT leave a single static image on screen for more than 6 seconds — split into multiple shots (one per entity, or mix image+video). >8s causes literal freeze frames
